component: wolfSSL, native certificate verification on Apple platforms
root_cause: In ProcessPeerCerts, the Apple native trust-store fallback ran on any non-zero certificate verification result and replaced it with its own verdict, so a native success also cleared hostname, OCSP and CRL failures already recorded; the fix runs the fallback only for ASN_NO_SIGNER_E and passes the expected domain name into the native SSL policy.
notes: fixed_ref is the merge commit of PR #8833; the fix spans commits 9864959 (domain name policy) and bc8eeea (only override ASN_NO_SIGNER_E). First released in wolfSSL 5.8.2. Only builds with WOLFSSL_SYS_CA_CERTS and WOLFSSL_APPLE_NATIVE_CERT_VALIDATION are affected (the latter is on by default for non-macOS Apple targets); the code sits behind Apple-only preprocessor guards, so a source-only audit is the practical test. src/internal.c is very large; if it does not fit one session, hand over its TLS peer certificate processing code.

root_cause: serverAuthenticate cached PublicKeyCallback results for up to 16 keys per connection and, when the client then signed with a key found in the cache, accepted it without calling the callback again, so the last key passed to PublicKeyCallback was not necessarily the key that authenticated and applications that authorized on that key could be bypassed; the fix shrinks the cache to one entry so the last callback always matches the authenticating key.
notes: Tag v0.31.0 points at the fix commit. The authorization bypass happens in applications that misuse the callback; the library-level question is whether a callback result is bound to the key that finally authenticates. Retest on the library (ssh/); optionally also on an application that records the key inside PublicKeyCallback.

component: Infineon cryptographic library (YubiKey 5, YubiHSM 2 and others)
root_cause: ECDSA signing in Infineon's cryptographic library computed the modular inverse of the nonce with a non-constant-time extended Euclidean algorithm and no blinding, so electromagnetic emanations during the inversion leaked information about the nonce and hence the private key.
notes: Event name EUCLEAK. Closed source (Infineon library inside secure-element firmware): question-level test only. Affected YubiKey 5 series firmware before 5.7.0 and YubiHSM 2 before 2.4.0, among other Infineon-based devices; Yubico's firmware 5.7.0 replaced the Infineon library with its own. Root cause taken from the NinjaLab paper and the vendor advisory, not from source.

classes: Values that must not be guessable
root_cause: bx seed produced wallet seed entropy through new_seed and pseudo_random_fill, which drew from a std::mt19937 Mersenne Twister seeded only by a clock value truncated to 32 bits (get_clock_seed), so a requested 128 to 256 bits of entropy held at most 32 bits; upstream did not fix the generator but turned bx seed into an obsolete command that always fails.
audit_scope: libbitcoin-explorer v3.6.0 src/ together with libbitcoin-system v3.6.0 src/utility/
notes: Event name Milk Sad. The weak generator lives in the dependency https://github.com/libbitcoin/libbitcoin-system (path prefixed libbitcoin-system/ above; read at tag v3.6.0); the clock-seeded mt19937 was introduced there by commit 6d5a06e283d81260165e0eab95175069bf03b408 ('Make random number generation thread safe and optimized'), which replaced per-call std::random_device use. fixed_ref is the merge of PR #729 into the version3 branch (2023-08-13); it only makes bx seed return an obsolete-command error, and the maintainers dispute the CVE. The recorded hit came from specialties 4.4 'Randomness and unpredictability'; the facet 'Values that must not be guessable' was added after this round, so it was not part of that judgment.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: EC.prototype.sign converted the message to a big number (BN) without checking its type or sign and signed that value, but derived the RFC 6979 nonce from its byte-array form (msg.toArray()), and because different BN values such as negative or non-canonical inputs can give the same bytes, two different signed values could share a nonce; the fix validates the input type, rejects negative values and asserts that the nonce input converts back to the same BN.
notes: No CVE assigned. The fix commit is a 'Merge commit from fork' (private security fork); its first parent is the mainline before the fix. Released as 6.6.1.

root_cause: JsonWebSignature deserialization (compact and JSON) verified the signature without processing the crit header, so tokens that marked header parameters the library does not understand as critical were accepted instead of rejected as RFC 7515 section 4.1.11 requires; the fix requires crit to be an integrity-protected list of strings whose names are present in the header and known (registered or configured as private) and rejects the token otherwise.
notes: fixed_ref is the merge of branch fix-jose-crit; 55e8517 is one of its commits (reject unprotected crit, enforce type). Release commit 09a51855747c13771a74958e233a6bf1fd143741 (1.6.4) follows directly. The fix also added the error class InvalidCritHeaderParameterNameError in errors.py.

component: Microsoft Entra ID, legacy Azure AD Graph
root_cause: Legacy Azure AD Graph accepted an unsigned impersonation token that wrapped a signed Actor token and named a user in another tenant, without checking that the tenant which issued the Actor token was the tenant being accessed; Microsoft added the tenant check and stopped issuing Actor tokens for Azure AD Graph.
notes: Closed-source cloud service fixed server-side in July 2025 (CVE published 2025-09-04): question-level test only. Root cause taken from the researcher's write-up and the MSRC entry.

component: The RADIUS protocol and its implementations
root_cause: RADIUS authenticates Access-Accept and Access-Reject responses only with the Response Authenticator, an ad hoc MD5 construction over the packet and the shared secret, and leaves the HMAC-based Message-Authenticator attribute optional outside EAP, so an implementation that accepts responses without Message-Authenticator can be given a response forged through an MD5 chosen-prefix collision; implementations fixed it by requiring and verifying Message-Authenticator on Access-* packets and limiting Proxy-State.
notes: Event name Blast-RADIUS. Protocol design flaw (RFC 2865) fixed separately in every implementation; FreeRADIUS v3.2.x is used here as the open reference implementation. The FreeRADIUS fix spans many commits between release_3_2_4 and release_3_2_5 (an OpenEmbedded backport cites the upstream range 3a00a6ecc188629b0441fd45ad61ca8986de156e..da643f1edc267ce95260dc36069e6f1a7a4d66f8, touching src/lib/radius.c and src/main/{client,listen,process,realms,mainconfig}.c among others); only 3a00a6e (global require_message_authenticator) was read. Symbols are where Message-Authenticator presence and the Response Authenticator are checked at release_3_2_4, not taken from the patch.

component: UEFI firmware from many vendors (AMI reference code)
root_cause: Production firmware shipped the Secure Boot Platform Key from AMI's reference implementation, a test key marked untrusted and not for shipping whose private key had leaked, because vendors never replaced the default key with their own before release.
notes: Event name PKfail. Closed-source vendor firmware: question-level test only. Fix is per-vendor firmware updates that install a vendor-owned Platform Key. Root cause taken from the CERT/CC note and Binarly's advisory.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: When unwrapping confidential GSS krb5 wrap tokens, gss_krb5int_unseal_token_v3 and gss_krb5int_unseal_v3_iov used the Extra Count field from the plaintext token header without comparing it with the copy of the header protected inside the encrypted data, so a modified Extra Count could truncate the recovered plaintext; the fix compares the decrypted header's Extra Count with the outer one and checks that the plaintext is long enough.
notes: 55fbf435 is the cherry-pick on the 1.21 release branch (fixed in 1.21.3); b0a2f8a5 is the original commit on master. The same commit also fixes CVE-2024-37371 (invalid reads from bad length fields, in src/lib/gssapi/krb5/k5unsealiov.c kg_unseal_iov_token); a report that finds only that one does not count for this sample.

component: MongoDB Server (protocol parsing, exploited in the wild)
root_cause: ZlibMessageCompressor::decompressData returned the output buffer length, which was sized from the uncompressed length the message header declared, instead of the number of bytes zlib actually produced, so the size check in decompressMessage always passed and uninitialized heap bytes after the real data were parsed as message content and could be sent back; the fix returns the real decompressed length so short messages are rejected.
notes: Event name MongoBleed. Reachable before authentication; exploited in the wild. Fixed in 8.2.3, 8.0.17, 7.0.28, 6.0.27, 5.0.32 and 4.4.30; release-branch backports have other hashes. The size check in decompressMessage already existed and was defeated by the wrong return value, not missing.

component: PostgreSQL libpq and psql (query and protocol parsing)
classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: PQescapeLiteral, PQescapeIdentifier, PQescapeString, PQescapeStringConn and the fe_utils helpers fmtId and appendStringLiteral took a multibyte character's length from its first byte and copied the following bytes unchecked, without verifying that the character was valid and complete, so psql could split an invalid sequence at different boundaries and a quote could end the quoted string; the fix verifies the encoding and replaces invalid or truncated characters with a byte sequence the server always rejects.
notes: Fix series on master, all marked CVE-2025-1094: 4dc2896 (add pg_encoding_set_invalid), 3e98c8c (explicit encoding for fmtId, adds fmtIdEnc), 5dc1e42 (core fix in the escaping functions). vulnerable_ref is the commit before the series. Backpatched through 13 with other hashes; fixed in 17.3, 16.7, 15.11, 14.16 and 13.19. The advisory's injectable case needs psql as the downstream parser (for example BIG5 client encoding with EUC_TW or MULE_INTERNAL server encoding). At vulnerable_ref, fmtId has no encoding argument; fmtIdEnc exists only from 3e98c8c.

root_cause: The query cache key built in executeQueryImpl and checked in QueryCache held only the query AST and the user name, not the user ID or the current roles, so after the same user switched roles (or a user was dropped and recreated under the same name) cached results computed under other row policies were returned; the fix keys and checks cache entries by user ID and current role set.
notes: fixed_ref is the merge commit of PR #58611 into master (2024-01-11); its first parent 4c5884b1d9c25c19172bc408948db01968eb8d74 still builds the key from context->getUserName(). Patched in 24.1.1.2048, 23.12.6.19, 23.8.12.13 and 23.3.22.3. Only matters when the query cache is enabled.

root_cause: isAllowedBySessionPolicy and isAllowedBySessionPolicyForServiceAccount evaluated the session (inline) policy with the caller's DenyOnly flag, which self-service operations set so that only explicit denies are checked, so a service account or STS credential restricted by a session policy could perform self operations such as creating a new service account that is free of the session policy and holds the parent's full permissions; the fix checks the session policy for an explicit allow whenever one is present.
notes: Fixed in RELEASE.2025-10-15T17-29-55Z (Go pseudo-version 0.0.0-20251015170045-c1a49490c78e). Whether the two functions are methods or package functions was not checked; search cmd/iam.go by name.

component: Apache Kafka (dual-write period of the ZooKeeper to KRaft migration)
root_cause: During the ZooKeeper-to-KRaft migration dual-write phase, KRaftMigrationZkWriter.handleAclsDelta wrote only the ACL changes in a metadata delta to ZooKeeper, where each resource's ACL set is stored and overwritten as a whole, so after an ACL was deleted the resource's remaining ACLs were not all written back and ZK-mode brokers enforced an incomplete set; the fix computes each changed resource's complete ACL set from the metadata image before writing it.
notes: The fix is titled 'MINOR: Fix some MetadataDelta handling issues during ZK migration' on trunk. Affected 3.5.0 to 3.6.1, fixed in 3.6.2 (the 3.6 branch backport has another hash, not looked up). Only matters while ZK-mode brokers are still running during migration. The ZooKeeper-side writer that replaces the whole ACL node lives under core/src/main/scala/kafka/zk/migration/; add it to the scope if the auditor needs the ZooKeeper storage semantics.

root_cause: luaY_parser created the chunk-name string and passed it to the lexer only as a raw pointer without anchoring it on the Lua stack, so a garbage collection during parsing could free it and the lexer then used a dangling pointer; the fix pushes the string onto the stack before parsing and pops it afterwards.
notes: Event name RediShell. The bug is in the Lua 5.1 copy vendored under deps/lua. Fixed in 8.2.2, 8.0.4, 7.4.6, 7.2.11 and 6.2.20; release-branch backports have other hashes. Needs an authenticated user allowed to run Lua scripts.

root_cause: Trusted PL/Perl's interpreter setup (plperl_trusted_init running plc_trusted.pl) left %ENV as Perl's magic hash bound to the real process environment, so unprivileged function code could set variables such as PATH that stayed in the backend process after the function ended and were later used by the server running as the database service account; the fix replaces %ENV in trusted PL/Perl with a tied copy whose store, delete and clear operations only warn.
notes: 3ebcfa54 is the commit on REL_17_STABLE (fixed in 17.1); backpatched through 12 with other hashes, for example REL_16_STABLE 8fe3e697a1a83a722b107c7cb9c31084e1f4d077 and REL_13_STABLE e428cd058f0bebb5782b0c263565b0ad088e9650; the master commit was not looked up. Untrusted plperlu keeps a writable %ENV on purpose.

root_cause: With TLS enabled on the server but no net.tls.CAFile configured, incoming connections skipped peer certificate validation instead of using the system CA store or refusing to start; the fix makes startup fail unless a CA file or the new tlsUseSystemCA parameter is given.
notes: Fix commit not found: the Jira ticket links none, and the commits OSV lists for this CVE are unrelated changes. Refs are 7.0-series release tags (also fixed in 6.0.14, 5.0.25 and 4.4.29; affected since 3.2.6). Comparing ssl_options_server.cpp at r7.0.5 and r7.0.6 shows the new startup check that rejects TLS without a chain of trust; the code that skipped server-side peer validation without a CA file (expected in src/mongo/util/net/ssl_manager_openssl.cpp) was not located, so paths and symbols give the place of the missing startup check only.

component: PostgreSQL pg_dump and psql (backup and restore)
root_cause: pg_dump, pg_dumpall and pg_restore wrote plain-text dumps as psql scripts in which data and definitions from the source server were not kept apart from psql meta-command interpretation, so a superuser of the source server could make dump content run as psql meta-commands on the restoring client; the fix adds psql \restrict and \unrestrict with a random key and makes the dump tools emit \restrict before any source data.
notes: 71ea0d6 is the master commit; backpatched through 13 with other hashes, for example REL_18_STABLE 67a2fbb8f9e9f75df08208e75da412c43a814688 and REL_14_STABLE e4998d089d903da6114209ae36da747b195375ca; fixed in 17.6, 16.10, 15.14, 14.19 and 13.22. The flaw is in the dump format design rather than one function; the symbols are where the fix inserts \restrict and \unrestrict. The related CVE-2025-8715 (newlines in object names in pg_dump comments) was fixed by a separate commit in the same release.

root_cause: Redis kept queuing replies such as NOAUTH errors to clients that had not authenticated, and checkClientOutputBufferLimits applied no limit to normal clients under the default client-output-buffer-limit, so an unauthenticated peer that never read replies could grow its output buffer until memory ran out; the fix disconnects unauthenticated clients whose output buffer exceeds 1024 bytes.
notes: Affects 2.6 and later; fixed in 7.4.3, 7.2.8 and 6.2.18 (branch backports have other hashes). The 1024-byte cap is a fixed constant in the fix, not a configuration option.
